_comment: Questions a person answers to fill team.json. 'required' ones decide whether a forecast is trustworthy. 'suggest' values are offered as choices (the person can always type another number). mine_history.py pre-fills suggestions where history can tell; the person confirms or overrides.

questions.ask: How many people will author pull requests (working with an agent) on this work at the same time?
questions.why: Sets how many PRs open per day, so it also sets review load. Adding authors without reviewers makes the review queue unstable.

questions.ask: How many focused hours per working day does each author spend on this work (not counting meetings)?
questions.why: Converts author effort hours into elapsed working days.

questions.ask: Of those hours, what fraction is really free for THIS backlog (the rest goes to other work, support, leave)?
questions.why: A second time factor on top of hours per day. 0.7 means 30% of the time goes elsewhere, so every author hour takes 1/0.7 as long to appear.

questions.ask: How many people review pull requests for this work? (0 means PRs merge with no independent review.)
questions.why: Review is an M/M/c queue: c is this number. With 0 there is no review wait and no rework in the forecast.

questions.ask: How many hours per working day does a reviewer work on this project in total (reviewing and everything else)?
questions.why: Together with the next answer it sets how much review time exists per day.

questions.ask: What fraction of a reviewer's day goes to reviewing this team's PRs (the rest is their own authoring and other work)?
questions.why: Reviewer capacity = hours per day x this fraction. Reviewers who also author have a small fraction.

questions.ask: How many days per week does the team work on this?
questions.why: Converts working days to calendar days and decides how much a night or weekend of unattended agent time is worth.

questions.ask: While the agent works on a story, how much of that time must the author stay with it?
questions.why: 1 = interactive (the author is steering, so the agent's run time uses the author's hours). 0 = background runs that finish overnight without the author.

questions.ask: How often does merged work reach its deployed state, in working days? (0 = every merge deploys immediately.)
questions.why: A merged PR waits for the next release batch: uniformly between 0 and this many days.

questions.ask: When a story is blocked on a decision (an owner must answer), how long does the answer usually take, in working days?
questions.why: Sets the wait for each open question; the owners are not the authors, so this wait uses no author time.

questions.ask: How many stories can one author keep in flight at once (agent running while they start another)?
questions.why: Used by plan.py to cap work in progress. Attended agent work cannot overlap, so this matters when agent runs are partly unattended.

questions.ask: How long does an author spend reading and steering the agent's output per attempt, besides being present during the run?
questions.why: Author effort per attempt.

questions.ask: On average, how many author hours go into one pull request?
questions.why: With the number of authors it sets PR arrivals (the review load) unless a measured PR rate is given.

questions.ask: How many PRs does this team open per working day? (Leave to derive it from authors and hours per PR.)
questions.why: A measured rate overrides the derived one.

questions.ask: How many changed lines can a reviewer get through per hour of review?
questions.why: Review effort per PR = diff lines / this. Mechanical moves are reviewed by proof, not line by line.

questions.ask: What is a typical (mean) PR size in changed lines?
questions.why: Sets reviewer service rate.

questions.ask: How many hours of human-equivalent work does the agent complete per hour it runs?
questions.why: Scales scope hours into agent run time.

questions.ask: How long does CI and verification take per attempt (wall clock)?
questions.why: Added to every attempt.

questions.ask: How long does triaging a failed attempt take an author?
questions.why: Author effort per retry.

questions.ask: How long does a deploy itself take once a release batch starts?
questions.why: Added after the batch wait.

questions.ask: Which focused-hours scale should story sizes use? (Focused hours: one person working with the agent from starting the branch to a pull request ready for review, with no waiting.)
questions.why: Turns a story's size (S, M, L, XL) into the focused hours the estimate starts from. It is your input, not a measurement; the presets are starting points.

questions.ask: Do your focused-hour sizes already include retries and steering (as measured actuals do), or are they the hours of one clean attempt?
questions.why: 1 scopes each attempt at the focused hours divided by the expected attempts, so the model's retries bring the total back to the focused hours. 0 lets the model add its own retries on top (the safer, longer reading).

questions.ask: What is a typical (median) pull request size, in changed lines?
questions.why: A story's diff size is its number of PRs times this, unless the story gives its own. It drives review effort and rework probability.
